descriptionChirho: The nominal sense of ken meaning 'gnat, louse' — a small biting or parasitic insect, specifically the creature of the third plague in Egypt; Arabic بَعُوض (ba'udh) 'mosquito/gnat'; Korean 이들 (ideul) 'lice'; Spanish piojos 'lice' and piojo 'louse'; Hindi जूएं (juen) 'lice'; Swahili chawa 'lice.' Used in Ex 8:13-14 [Heb 8:13-14] for the plague of lice/gnats that Aaron brought forth from the dust, with both singular and plural forms. The construct and articled forms (the gnats, gnats of) are grammatical variants of the same insect referent.

The adverbial sense of ken meaning 'so, thus' — a manner adverb indicating conformity or agreement with what precedes; Arabic ذَلِكَ (dhalika) 'that/so'; Korean 같이 (gachi) 'likewise'; Spanish así 'thus/so'; Hindi ही (hi) emphatic particle; Swahili hivyo 'thus.' This single occurrence functions as a demonstrative adverb pointing to a previously stated manner or state of affairs, completely distinct from the nominal 'gnat/louse' homonym that shares the same consonantal form.
